subject: DPA + SCCs: HarborCare redline coordination and evidence timeline
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@harborcare.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborcare.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft DPA + SCCs — our initial redlines

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the call this morning. We're attaching our initial redlines to the DPA and a short summary of hosting region concerns. High-level asks from legal and privacy:

- Confirm whether Redwood can commit to EU-hosted processing for HarborCare PII (we need region gating for prod).
- Clarify subprocessors and KMS ownership — suggest KMS key management as customer-managed for EU data.
- We're proposing updates to the liability cap in Section 7.3 tied to data breach reimbursements.
- Add a Transfer Impact Addendum to preserve SCCs compatibility and list fallback routing.

Attached: HarborCare_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)

Can you get privacy/legal to review and tell us what evidence (SOC2, subprocessor list, export controls) you can provide by next Tue (2026-09-15)? We want to finalize order form signoff the week after.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director of Legal Ops
HarborCare

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@harborcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborcare.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs — our initial redlines

Thanks Sam — received and uploaded. Quick update from Redwood side:

- EU processing: We can commit to EU-hosting for production environments. We'll document region routing and create a Transfer Impact Addendum as you suggested.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys are available for Dedicated and Private deployments only; for Hosted API we can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via our KMS integration but with some operational constraints. We can spell this out in an exhibit.
- Subprocessors: I'll send the current subprocessor list and our SCCs mapping spreadsheet.
- Liability cap: need Ben/legal to weigh in on language — I'll loop him in for redline suggestions.

Action items:
1) Ben: propose compromise language for 7.3 (liability) + indemnity carveouts for data incidents.
2) Irene: confirm list of artifacts we can provide by 2026-09-15 (SOC2 summary, whitepaper on export controls, subprocessor matrix).
3) Nikhil/Tom: schedule 30m alignment call for 9/14 to walk redlines and operational mitigations.

I'll attach the SCCs matrix once Ben and Irene confirm.

— Nikhil
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@harborcare.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborcare.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs — our initial redlines

Hi all,

Reviewed HarborCare's redlines (thanks for the clear markup). I sketched compromise language inline in the attached matrix and called out three negotiation points that typically drag:

1) Liability cap tied to breach reimbursement: propose a split-cap approach — general contract cap remains as-is; a separate data-breach bucket (reasoned multiple of fees) with narrow carveouts for gross negligence.
2) BYOK / KMS: for Hosted API we'll offer BYOK for encryption-in-transit and at-rest metadata keys; however, full customer-managed HSM for tokenization requires Dedicated/Private. Add an explanatory exhibit with operational trade-offs.
3) Transfer Impact Addendum / SCCs: we'll provide a draft annex listing the transfer routes and fallback behaviors; HarborCare will confirm the permitted routing rules.

Attachments: Redwood_SCCs_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (pdf)

Proposed timeline:
- 9/14: 30m alignment call (confirming)
- 9/15: Redwood to drop final evidence pack (SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, SCCs annex draft)
- 9/17: HarborCare to confirm whether liability restructure is acceptable; if not, narrow scope for escalation.

If HarborCare needs faster exec approval on liability carveouts, let's identify the exact items for escalation (credits, SLA credits, additional audit windows).

Ben Carter
VP, Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@harborcare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborcare.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs — our initial redlines (follow-up)

Ben — thanks for the clear proposals and the SCCs matrix. Quick notes after internal review:

- The split-cap approach is acceptable in principle; our CFO needs the concrete numeric bucket. Can Redwood propose a numeric multiple tied to 12 months of committed fees for the data-breach bucket?
- BYOK sounds workable for Hosted for the metadata you mentioned; we need a short exhibit that explains key rotation impacts and rollback windows for token revocation.
- For the Transfer Impact Addendum, we'll review the SCCs annex draft and provide permitted routing rules by 9/20.

Pending items we expect from Redwood by end of day 9/15: subprocessor list, SOC2 summary, SCCs annex draft, and the proposed numeric for the breach bucket (ballpark). Please confirm attachments will be in Drive and share links.

If everything aligns, procurement is aiming for order form signature the week of 9/27. Otherwise we'll flag specific escalation points.

Best regards,
Samantha Lee
Director of Legal Ops, HarborCare
